option_relations.rationale: Option A describes a left thalamic intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension, which is a broader category encompassing the more specific diagnosis of acute hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage in the left thalamus and corona radiata causing right hemiplegia and right facial palsy.
The vignette describes a left-sided hemorrhage causing right-sided symptoms, not an ipsilateral hemisphere hemorrhagic stroke. The facial paralysis is central, not peripheral type.

Option C describes hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage, which is a broader category that includes the specific diagnosis of acute hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage in the left thalamus and corona radiata causing right hemiplegia and right facial palsy.

Option D, 'Left hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (thalamus–corona radiata region)', is clinically equivalent to the leaf 'Acute hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage in left thalamus and corona radiata causing right hemiplegia and right facial palsy', as it specifies the same location and etiology of the hemorrhage.
